title: The 10 Best Corded Reciprocating Saws
subtitle: Wired demo saws ranked from live Amazon data — endless power for cutting, pruning, and tear-out.
intro: A reciprocating saw (a.k.a. Sawzall) rips a long blade back and forth through wood, metal, PVC, nail-embedded lumber, and tree branches — the go-to for demolition and rough cuts. Corded models give you full, sustained power for the least money and never run flat, which matters when you're tearing out a wall or bucking a pile of branches. Amps are the number to watch: 7-8 amps handles most jobs, and 10-13 amps is heavy demolition. Want to cut anywhere with no cord? See the cordless list.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMES300 7.5-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: The best all-around corded recip for most people. A balanced 7.5-amp CRAFTSMAN with a full 1-1/8" stroke, tool-free blade change, and 4.7 stars — enough power for pruning and remodeling without the weight of a demolition saw.

products.name: SKIL 9206-02 7.5-Amp Variable Speed Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: The value pick — a genuine 7.5-amp corded recip with variable speed and a tool-free blade change for around $55, backed by 1,900 reviews. Everything a homeowner needs to demo and prune, nothing they don't.

products.name: DEWALT DWE305 12-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: The most powerful, best-reviewed corded recip here — a 12-amp DEWALT with a 4-position blade clamp (cut flush or at angles) and 3,900 reviews at 4.8 stars. If price is no object and you want a demolition workhorse, this is it.
pros: 4-position blade clamp for flush and angled cuts

products.name: SKIL 13-Amp Reciprocating Saw with Buzzkill Anti-Vibration
products.verdict: The most amps here (13) plus Buzzkill anti-vibration tech that noticeably reduces hand fatigue on long cuts. A smooth, powerful pick if you'll run it for hours.

products.name: SKIL 9216-01 9-Amp Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: More motor than the budget saws for a small step up in price — a 9-amp SKIL with variable speed and a tool-free blade change. A smart middle ground under $75.
pros: 9-amp motor, more power for the price

products.name: WEN 3630 10-Amp 8-Position Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: WEN's value formula — a real 10-amp motor and an 8-position rotating handle for cutting at awkward angles, all for around $53. A lot of power per dollar from a known value brand.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 7-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: A simple, light 7-amp corded recip from a trusted home brand, with a removable tool-free blade clamp. Fine for pruning, PVC, and light demolition around the house.
pros: Light and easy for a corded saw
cons: 7 amps is light for heavy demo

products.name: BOSCH GSA12-30 12-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: Bosch pro build in a 12-amp corded package, with a long 1-3/16" stroke for aggressive cutting. Newer to Amazon, but Bosch's reputation and stroke length make it a serious demo saw.

products.name: Makita JR3051T 12-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw
products.verdict: A pro-grade Makita with a big 1-1/4" stroke and a tool-less blade clamp — a longtime favorite of tradespeople for tearing through framing and metal. Sold here in a renewed listing.

products.name: 7-Amp Corded Reciprocating Saw (with blades)
products.verdict: The budget floor for a full-size corded recip — a 7-amp saw that ships with blades for under $50. No brand pedigree, but for occasional wood, PVC, and tree pruning it does the job.

avoid.name: Ingersoll Rand 529 3/8" Reciprocating Air Saw
avoid.flag: It's a pneumatic AIR saw — needs a compressor, no wall plug
avoid.verdict: A quality pro saw — but it's pneumatic. It doesn't plug into a wall outlet; it runs on compressed air and needs a good-sized shop compressor. Buy it only if you already have one.
reasons: It runs on compressed air, not electricity. There's no cord to plug in — you need an air compressor and hose to use it at all.
It wants real CFM, so a small hobby compressor won't run it; the true cost is the saw plus a capable compressor.
If you want to plug into a wall outlet and start cutting, buy the DEWALT DWE305 or the SKIL 9206 above instead.
It's on this 'avoid' list only because it's the wrong category for someone shopping electric reciprocating saws — in a shop with air, it's fine.

buyers_guide.a: It pushes a blade back and forth for fast, rough cuts through wood, metal, PVC, drywall, and nail-embedded lumber, plus pruning branches. It's the demolition and remodeling saw — not for fine straight cuts (that's a circular saw).

A corded saw gives full, sustained power for the least money and never runs out of charge — best for tear-outs, long cutting sessions, and a keep-forever demo saw. The trade is the cord and needing an outlet.
7-8 amps handles most home demolition and pruning. 10-13 amps is heavy-duty for tearing through framing, thick metal, and long jobs. More amps means more power and usually more weight.
Yes. A longer stroke (1-1/8 to 1-1/4 inch) uses more of the blade and cuts faster and more aggressively — better for demolition. Shorter strokes are smoother and easier one-handed.

buyers_guide.q: Tool-free blade change and orbital action?
buyers_guide.a: Tool-free blade change lets you swap blades without a wrench — get it; every pick here has it. Orbital action adds an oval blade motion for even faster wood cutting; it's a nice extra on higher-end saws but not essential.
